name_zh: 图克瓦尔茶园大吉岭红茶
cultivar: Mainly clonal and China bushes, including AV2
processing: Darjeeling tea made across the flushes, with first flush black tea the best known, and second flush, autumn and green teas also made.
harvest_season: First flush in spring is the garden's best-known picking; second flush and autumn lots follow.
appearance_dry: Typically green-tinged olive leaf with pale tips in first flush lots, browner in later ones.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, deeper amber later in the year.
appearance_wet: Bright green and copper leaf in spring lots.
taste_profile: Typical of fine first flush Darjeeling, expect a floral, brisk cup; the garden's own notes are mostly seller descriptions, so taste with an open mind.

brewing.notes: For first flush lots, use cooler water and do not over-steep. Later flushes take a few more degrees.

vintage_note: Today the tea is mostly sold under the Puttabong name, by year and flush. First flush lots are the most sought after and are best drunk young.
description:
Tukvar is one of Darjeeling's founding tea names, tied to the start of commercial planting in the district. The estate is now generally known as Puttabong, so the old name is more likely to appear in history than on a shop label.

It grows mainly clonal and China bushes at around 2,000 metres. Its reputation rests on first flush black tea, including a clonal lot from AV2 bushes sold as Puttabong Clonal Queen, and it also makes later flush and green teas.

Typical of high first flush Darjeeling, the spring cup is floral and brisk. Brew it cooler and shorter than you would a summer tea, and go by taste rather than the clock.

Do not confuse it with North Tukvar, listed as a separate estate also called Singla. If a label says just Tukvar, ask which garden is meant.
history:
Commercial production at Tukvar is usually dated to 1852, and accounts differ on whom to credit: one names Captain Masson, another Dr Campbell, and a third says experimental planting preceded commercial output in 1856. The Lebong Tea Company is also linked with its start.

The estate is now called Puttabong. The Jayshree Group, which acquired it in 1967, owns and runs it.
